problem: Pretrained vision-and-language models used in VLN (OSCAR, PREVALENT) are trained on web-crawled or generic data, leaving a domain gap with indoor VLN scenes. As a result they align object- and scene-level semantics poorly with instructions.
motivation: A VLN agent needs to ground objects and scenes named in instructions onto its visual perception, and the quality of the pretrained representation strongly affects navigation. Full retraining is costly, so the paper uses cheap prompt tuning to inject indoor visual knowledge into a frozen encoder.
key_idea: Learn soft visual prompts on the input of a frozen pretrained visual encoder, using CLIP-generated in-domain (Matterport3D) image-text pseudo labels, to adapt the model to VLN scenes before downstream fine-tuning.
insight: The gains come from injecting in-domain object and scene semantics into the visual encoder. The gain is larger for OSCAR (web-pretrained: R2R val-unseen SR +3.42, SPL +3.18) than for PREVALENT (already trained on VLN data: SR +1.76, SPL +1.79), which supports the domain-gap explanation. The same prompts work on both backbones, so the approach is model-agnostic.
method: Pseudo-label generation: sample about 1000 Matterport3D indoor images, use CLIP with the template 'A photo of a {object}' over object and scene class names, and pick the highest-similarity text as the label.
Soft visual prompts: 10 learnable d-dimensional vectors are inserted into the input space of the visual encoder's first layer and propagated through the N layers.
Prompt tuning: the PREVALENT backbone is frozen; only the prompts and an MLP head on the output [CLS] are trained with cross-entropy classification (20 epochs, batch size 10).

Downstream VLN: the prompt-augmented visual encoder feeds a RecBERT agent (initialized from PREVALENT or OSCAR), which is fine-tuned on R2R (300k iterations, batch size 8) and REVERIE (200k iterations, batch size 8).
Model-agnosticism check: the same prompt tuning is applied to OSCAR-initialized RecBERT.

setting.backbone: RecBERT with PREVALENT/OSCAR-initialized encoder; frozen visual encoder + learned soft prompts, then fine-tuned
setting.training_data: About 1000 CLIP-pseudo-labelled Matterport3D image-text pairs for prompt tuning, then R2R / REVERIE training data (no other extra data)

results: DAP reaches R2R val-unseen SR 65 / SPL 59 and test-unseen SR 64 / SPL 59, beating the RecBERT (init. PREVALENT) baseline by about 1-2 points and the newer ADAPT and GRVLN-BERT. On REVERIE test-unseen it improves RGS by 1.03 and RGSPL by 1.27 over RecBERT (PREVALENT).
limitations: Gains over the RecBERT baseline are small (about 1-2 points) and there is no significance or seed-variance analysis.
Only prompts on the visual encoder are studied, and only two backbones (OSCAR, PREVALENT) and two benchmarks; no ablation on the number of prompts, dataset size or pseudo-label quality.
Pseudo labels come from CLIP zero-shot classification and may be noisy; the label vocabulary is not detailed.
